A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RAC research, with matching algorithms, experiments, and figures. All 10 pages of v1 and 13 pages of v2, including their appendices, support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original pruning accuracy, runtime, reconstruction-error, calibration, and throughput experiments in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds Qwen3, DeepSeek-R1-Llama, AIME-25, and alternative-pruner results.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same collection of prompt and dense-model-generated CoT activations, concatenation, and layer-wise pruning. The empirical RAC reconstruction loss is unchanged. Testing ALPS and WANDA exercises the existing pruning interface without introducing a new RAC component.

E1.justification: v2 adds AIME-25 competition-math evaluation in Tables 4 and 10. MATH500, LiveCodeBench, and the C4, Open-R1-Math-220K, and Codeforces calibration sources remain. This extends mathematical difficulty coverage within the existing math-and-coding scope.

E2.justification: v1 evaluates SparseGPT; ALPS and WANDA appear only as references or examples. v2 evaluates ALPS and WANDA on MATH500 in Table 9, compares them with SparseGPT results, and reports ALPS on AIME-25 in Table 10. The C4, prompt-only, and RAC calibration comparisons remain.

E3.justification: v2 substantially expands evaluated model configurations to Qwen3-1.7B/8B/14B and DeepSeek-R1-Llama-8B/70B, with new comparisons at 30–50% sparsity. The retained experiments still specify 1M calibration tokens, up to 8192 generated calibration tokens, and zero-shot evaluation with a 32k output budget.

E4.justification: The new 'Varying the pruning algorithm' analysis tests whether RAC's benefits depend on SparseGPT, using ALPS/WANDA on MATH500 and ALPS on AIME-25. This adds a substantive generality check. The original on/off-policy, structured-pruning/FP8, decoding-budget, and reconstruction-error analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report accuracy with standard errors. v2 adds no repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedure. Additional rows follow the existing reporting practice; changing some SE notation to parentheses is presentational.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results for new model configurations, AIME-25, and alternative pruners. New entries include Qwen3-8B MATH500 accuracy at 50% sparsity of 0.862 with SparseGPT+RAC and 0.940 with ALPS+RAC. All five original tables retain their numerical values after renumbering. Figure 1 changes the displayed 70%-sparsity runtime from approximately 9 hours to 8.4 hours.

T1.justification: v2 removes the explicit expected-loss minimization over dense-policy rollouts and layers presented in v1 Section 4. It retains the empirical RAC reconstruction identity, now Equation 7, and the decoding equations. This is a limited removal of formal exposition; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract's central RAC claim remains unchanged. v2's introduction adds explicit headline claims about pruning to 50% sparsity, retaining up to 95% of dense accuracy, and improving accuracy by up to 17% over existing pruning approaches. These quantify the contribution without replacing its central thesis.

C2.justification: v2 interprets Qwen3 results as evidence of broader applicability, AIME-25 results as supporting calibration alignment on harder problems, and the alternative-pruner results as showing algorithm-independent benefits and sometimes stronger ALPS performance. Existing mechanism explanations and limitations remain. The decoding-budget mitigation added to the limitations paragraph was already discussed in v1.

D1.justification: v2 newly states that all one-shot pruning experiments use a single H100 GPU and changes the printed code-repository address from RAC to Reasoning-Aware-Compression. These are documentation/access-information changes; the PDFs do not establish a hardware change or repository availability.

R1.justification: v2 adds a substantive comparison with Williams et al.'s self-calibration, distinguishing task-conditioned reasoning traces from unconditional generated text. It also adds pruning, C4, and sparse-hardware references while removing GPTQ, Liu's quantization study, and Zhu's compression survey. The existing positioning against calibration-selection and CoT-distillation work remains.

P1.justification: The introduction and pruning background receive targeted rewrites, the method gains a short overview, and the results discussion expands. Section 5.2 changes from 'Ablations' to 'Additional Experiments' and reorders analyses. The main section sequence and most method and retained-analysis prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a different conference layout, adds Tables 2–4 and 9–10, rearranges and reformats retained tables, and adds highlighting to appendix results. Figure 1 is redrawn with colored axes and revised scaling. Figure 2 retains the identical heatmap image but moves within the document.

improvement.justification: v1 supports RAC's broad applicability primarily through SparseGPT on DeepSeek-R1-Qwen models. v2 directly tests additional pruners, Qwen3 and Llama models, and harder AIME-25 problems, substantially addressing uncertainty about generality. The self-calibration comparison also clarifies novelty. Although added experiment settings remain briefly documented and statistical reporting does not improve, the broader validation materially strengthens the paper.
